title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Ops, Runbooks, Postmortems, Game Days, and Comms
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard incident lifecycle, severity taxonomy, runbook templates, postmortem expectations, on-call rotation rules, game day guidance, and canonical status page / customer communication templates. The goal is rapid detection, clear ownership, safe mitigation, and blameless learning.

Scope: production services supporting hosted API, dedicated inference, private deployments, control plane services, and ancillary systems (auth, billing, metrics).

1) Incident severity and routing

- Severity definitions (apply consistently across services):
  - Sev 1 (P0): Customer-facing outage or data loss affecting >5% of traffic or critical enterprise customers (slack: #prod-sev1, page: immediate). SLO impact: availability < 99.0% for >5m or latency P95 > 2s for >10m.
  - Sev 2 (P1): Major degradation (partial loss of functionality) or single-customer impacting error that blocks key workflows. SLO impact: availability 99.0–99.9% or latency P95 500ms–2s sustained >10m.
  - Sev 3 (P2): Minor degradation, isolated errors, or internal-only incidents.
  - Sev 4 (P3): Non-urgent operational tasks, configuration drift, or long-term improvements.

Routing rules:
- Pager duty flows: All Sev1/Sev2 incidents must page the on-call SRE and the service owner simultaneously.
- SEVs are declared by the on-call SRE, service owner, or support lead. If in doubt, escalate to Sev1.

2) Incident lifecycle (high-level steps)

1. Detection & Triage
   - Sources: synthetic alerts, SLO breaches, customer reports, monitoring (Prometheus, Datadog), paging, and on-call Slack.
   - Triage goal (10 min): confirm impact, scope, initial mitigation plan, and owner.
2. Mobilize (10–30 min)
   - Create incident channel (Slack #incident-<shortname>-<date>).
   - Define incident commander (IC), scribe, and primary on-call.
   - Post the initial incident summary to the channel and the status page draft.
3. Contain & Mitigate (15–120+ min)
   - Follow the runbook for the affected service. Apply safe mitigations first (traffic routing, fallback to model variants, increase autoscaling, revoke bad deployments).
   - If mitigation is not possible, execute escalations in the matrix below.
4. Recovery & Validate (after mitigation)
   - Confirm full or partial recovery via metrics and end-to-end tests.
   - Remove customer-facing mitigations in a controlled manner.
5. Post-incident (24–72 hours)
   - Draft and publish a blameless postmortem within 72 hours (initial incident timeline, root cause, mitigations, action items with owners and due dates).
   - Track action items in the engineering board and verify closure.

3) On-call rotations & responsibilities

- Teams: eng-sre, runtime, infra, api-platform, customer-success escalation.
- Rotation model: primary on-call (7-day rotation) + secondary (follow-the-sun backup) + weekend on-call (full-weekend handoff).
- Responsibilities of primary on-call:
  - Respond to pages within 5 minutes for Sev1 and 15 minutes for Sev2.
  - Triage alerts, declare incident severity, and assign IC if not self.
  - Maintain the health of runbooks and report runbook gaps.
- Handover checklist (end of shift): open incidents summary, outstanding action items, and any degraded services. Use the handoff template in Slack pinned message.

4) Runbook template (canonical)

Title: <service> — Incident Runbook
Service: <service name> (owner: <team>, pager: <pd escalation>)
SLOs: availability, latency thresholds (e.g., availability 99.9% monthly, p95 latency < 300ms)
Detection signals: list of metrics/alerts (Prometheus rule IDs or Datadog monitors)
Initial triage checklist (1–2 lines each):
  1. Confirm alert on Grafana dashboard: link to dashboard
  2. Verify synthetic checks and customer reports
  3. Check recent deploys (CI job IDs) and feature flags
  4. Look for correlated logs (ELK/Kibana) and error class distribution
Mitigation steps (safe-first ordering):
  1. Redirect traffic to healthy region: aws route53 / internal LB steps
  2. Scale replica count / increase pod resources (kubectl or k8s autoscaler)
     - Example: kubectl -n infra scale deployment runtime-inference --replicas=8
  3. Rollback last deployment if correlated (include CI job ID and rollback command)
  4. Disable specific feature flags via LaunchDarkly console
  5. Flush caches or restart connector processes
Post-recovery validation:
  - Run smoke tests: curl -sS https://api.redwood-inference.internal/health | jq .
  - Verify SLO metrics returned to baseline for 30 minutes
Owners & contacts:
  - Primary owner: <team email or Slack handle>
  - Secondary owner: <oncall backup>
  - Escalation path: oncall -> service-owner -> eng-managers -> VP Eng

5) Postmortem template (blameless)

- Title: Incident — <short description> (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Incident severity: SevX
- Summary: 2–3 sentence customer-facing summary.
- Timeline: ordered bullets with timestamps (UTC) covering detection, mitigation, and recovery.
- Root cause: concise technical root cause.
- Contributing factors: environment, process, monitoring gaps, human factors.
- Impact: services, customers, duration, and SLO delta.
- Immediate mitigations: what we did to restore service.
- Long-term actions: specific tasks, owners, and due dates. Each action must have an owner and a target completion date.
- Learnings & risk reductions: short section describing what changed in process or automation.
- Validation & follow-up: how we will verify the fix and which paged alerts will be retired or changed.

Postmortem cadence: draft within 72 hours, review with stakeholders within 7 days, and mark all action items closed or moved to backlog within 30 days.

6) Escalation matrix (quick reference)

Service owner escalation table (ASCII):

| Role | Pager/Slack | Response SLA | When to escalate |
|------|-------------|--------------|------------------|
| Primary on-call | PD / Slack @oncall | 5m (Sev1) | Cannot contain in 20m or requires cross-team work |
| Service owner | Slack @service-owner | 15m | Mitigation needs code change or deployment |
| Eng manager | Email/Slack | 30m | Requires business/priority decisions or incident >1h |
| VP Eng | Email/Phone | 1h | Major outage affecting key customers or >4h duration |

7) Game days (exercise guidance)

Purpose: validate runbooks, cross-team coordination, and automation under realistic load.
Frequency: quarterly per critical service, annual cross-service disaster recovery.
Format: planned injection window + blameless retrospective.
Example scenarios:
- Model-serving cold cache spike: simulate KV cache eviction and observe P95 latency increase.
- Control-plane loss: degrade metadata DB and verify fallback to cached routing.
- Region failover: move traffic from us-east-1 -> us-west-2 following runbook steps.
Success criteria:
- IC declared within 10 minutes, incident channel created, mitigation executed, and post-game learning captured.

8) Status page & customer communications templates

Status page guidance:
- Immediately publish an "investigating" post for Sev1/2 with short summary, affected systems, and expected next update time (default: 30 minutes).
- Update every 30 minutes for Sev1 until monitoring indicates recovery.
- Provide final incident summary when postmortem is published.

Templates (editable)
- Status page — Investigating (short):
  - Title: Investigating — API errors impacting request processing
  - Body: We are investigating elevated errors in the Redwood API that are impacting request processing for some customers. Our engineers are actively investigating. Next update: in 30 minutes.

- Status page — Mitigating (short):
  - Title: Mitigating — Traffic rerouted to healthy region
  - Body: We have identified the source of elevated errors and are routing traffic to a healthy region. Metrics indicate partial recovery. We will continue to monitor and provide an update within 30 minutes.

- Customer email / Slack template (for paid customers)
  - Subject: Incident (YYYY-MM-DD) — Partial outage impacting Redwood API
  - Body: Hello,

We are currently investigating an incident impacting the Redwood API. Some requests may fail or experience elevated latency. Our on-call engineers have identified the likely cause and are executing mitigations (traffic routing, rollback). We will update you within 30 minutes or sooner. If you need immediate assistance, reply to this email or contact your account team.

Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Operations

- Post-incident customer summary template (short):
  - Title: Incident Summary — (YYYY-MM-DD)
  - Body: Summary of impact, timeline, root cause, mitigations, and actions taken to reduce recurrence risk. Attach the public postmortem link.

9) Operational tooling, dashboards, and runbook maintenance

- Dashboards to maintain per service: availability, p95 latency, errors per minute, deploy frequency, recent rollbacks. Links should be included in each runbook.
- Monitor rules: define Prometheus/Datadog alert IDs in the runbook and guard alert noise via alert thresholds: e.g., errors > 5% of requests sustained for 5m triggers P1.
- Runbook ownership: each service must have a runbook with an owner and last_reviewed date. Runbook review cadence: quarterly.

10) Appendix: useful commands and example runbook snippet

- Example k8s scale: kubectl -n runtime scale deployment runtime-inference --replicas=8
- Rollback example (CI): ci rollback --job 12345 --service runtime-inference
- Health check: curl -sS https://api.redwood-inference.internal/health | jq .

Example runbook snippet:

-- runbook header --
Service: runtime-inference
Owner: runtime-team@redwood.com
SLOs: avail 99.9% monthly, p95 < 300ms
Detection: dd-monitor-8754 (error_rate > 3% for 5m)
Mitigation (first actions):
  1) Check Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/abc/runtime
  2) Scale deployment to 8 replicas: kubectl -n runtime scale deployment runtime-inference --replicas=8
  3) If errors persist, rollback to prior stable revision with CI job 12297

Closing notes:
- Keep communications factual and time-stamped. Use the incident channel to consolidate status and decisions; do not duplicate with multiple long email chains.
- Aim to publish a public-friendly summary within 72 hours and a technical postmortem within 7 days.

Contact & ownership
- On-call SRE: @oncall (pager duty)
- Incident comms lead: ops-comms@redwood.com
- Executive escalations: eng-exec-oncall@redwood.com
